# UI choreography

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

Product UI in motion: panels, cards, bento, lists and states that arrive front-loaded and keep the camera alive. 53 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Card lands by shrinking to size

`dv-oversize-card-settle` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · any

A notification, a widget or a hero card appears a little large (1.07-1.22x) and settles down to size while it sharpens; dashboard widgets can cut on every 4 f at 107 % and settle in 5 f; a full-frame photo can shrink 20 % into a card.

- **Build:** <Oversize from={1.12} dur={16}> or Words oversize on UI; widgets with starts every 8 f. Anatomy: Scale-down landing, defocus clearing; per-widget cut-ons on a fixed cadence. Sound: A whoosh tail; cork-like pops on the photo shrink. Materials: The result card's paragraph fades out line by line toward its end, as if still streaming (a vertical mask from opaque at 45 % to transparent), and a thin two-hue gradient rule echoing the ground separates it from the footer chips.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Oversize`
- **Materials:** The result card's paragraph fades out line by line toward its end, as if still streaming (a vertical mask from opaque at 45 % to transparent), and a thin two-hue gradient rule echoing the ground separates it from the footer chips.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** 10-38 f expo-out (47 % in 10 %); widgets 8 f apart, 10 f settle.
- **Use when:** Notifications, dashboards, cards that land on a beat.
- **Avoid when:** Overshooting below size.

### Card lands, the one before steps back

`ui-card-arrival-demotion` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · launch, update, feature, vertical

A new card arrives tilted and squares up on the same curve it travels on; the card already there scales down and moves up, half done exactly when the new one appears, so the stack reads as one push.

- **Build:** cardArrive(f, { start, from: { x, y, rot }, creep }, film) for the newcomer (position, rotation and scale share one curve); demote(f, { at: start, to: { scale: 0.82, y: -87 } }, film) for the card before. Or pass arrive / demote to <Card>.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards.cardArrive`, `fx/Cards.demote`
- **Timing:** Arrival 50 f on E.snapOut, tilt 8-35 deg at the start, creep 6-90 px/s afterwards. Demotion 20 f on E.whipBuild to x0.82 and 87 px up, centred on the arrival.
- **Use when:** Notifications, suggestions, a feed of results, a stack of options.
- **Avoid when:** More than three cards in one beat (it becomes a queue).

### Card scales in, creeps, then pushes into the cut

`dv-card-scale-in-creep-push` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · any

A card or dialog grows from 70-90 % (often blurred or smeared on its first frame) to full size with 90 % of the change in about 8 f, keeps a slow creep, then accelerates into the cut; a dock can expand out of a split line.

- **Build:** Cards enterState with scale from 0.85 + creep + scaleBreath into the cut. Anatomy: Scale 0.7-0.89 -> 1 expo-out, a 0.05 %/f creep or 1.8 px/f growth, quad-in push into the cut; optional relax of 0.8 % after the overshoot-free landing; content swaps 1 f. Sound: The cut on frame 1; none on the push.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Timing:** In 12-65 f; creep for the hold; push 32 f.
- **Use when:** Hero cards, export dialogs, posts, chat windows.
- **Avoid when:** Growing from zero.

### Cards dealt or dropped into a grid

`ui-card-grid-arrival` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · any

Cards land in a row or grid one after another, either dealt fast with a small tilt that squares up, or falling from just in front of the camera and shrinking into their slots.

- **Build:** Deal preset: card i appears at t0 + 5*i, its opacity stepping to 1 on the first frame while rotate goes 4 to 0 deg and scale 0.95 to 1 over 7 f on E.out, left to right, with no overshoot. Depth-drop preset: card i starts at delays [0, 4, 10, 14] (row-major, 6 extra frames between rows) and goes translateY 534 to 0 px and scale lmix(1.38, 1, p) on the same progress p over 54 f on E.out, half the distance in about 6 f at up to 62 px/f under the motion-blur pass. In the depth-drop keep each card's text and icons at opacity 0 until the card slows (prog(f, s + 8, s + 16, E.smooth)), so content resolves on landing below 20 px/f. Cards are opaque with a soft shadow (0 8px 30px at 6% black) and a radius of about 32 px at 1080p.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards.cardArrive`, `fx/Cards.Card`
- **Timing:** Deal: 5 f stagger, 7 f settle (E.out), rotate 4 deg, scale 0.95. Drop: 54 f (E.out), stagger 0/4/10/14 f, 534 px, scale 1.38 to 1, peak ~62 px/f, content fades in from +8 to +16 f.
- **Use when:** Revealing a set of options, results, features or integrations that should read as one set with a clear reading order.
- **Avoid when:** There is one hero object, or more than about 8 cards (use a row cascade or a scroll).

### Cards fan out from behind into a stack

`dv-card-fan-stack` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature

Copies of a card slide out from behind the front card 2 f apart into a tilted stack or a cover-flow fan; sibling cards enter from opposite sides with faint ghost trails; the stack collapses back behind the front card on exit.

- **Build:** Cards cardArrive per copy with delays 4 f and demote for the front card's lift. Anatomy: Followers 2 f apart, spreading on an ease-in to 42 px/f then a settle push x1.08; hero card lifts x1.25 while the fan spreads; tilt 2-8 deg; collapse on an ease-in. Sound: A pop on the spread; a whoosh series on the collapse. Materials: Before the back cards fan out, 1-3 hairline card edges appear one by one at the side of the single front card (one more every 4 f, a 1 px rim at 18 % white), so the viewer senses the stack before it opens.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Materials:** Before the back cards fan out, 1-3 hairline card edges appear one by one at the side of the single front card (one more every 4 f, a 1 px rim at 18 % white), so the viewer senses the stack before it opens.
- **Timing:** Spread 20 f; settle 16 f; siblings 40 f apart; collapse 22 f.
- **Use when:** Plans, sources, payments, posters: several of one kind.
- **Avoid when:** More than about five cards.

### Carousel: fast in, near stop, fast out

`dv-carousel-pass` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · any

A row of cards slides through: fast on entry, decaying almost to zero for the read, then accelerating before the cut, with soft faded edges; status chips can swap spinner to done left to right as it passes; or the row moves in discrete pushes as each new card lands.

- **Build:** A camera x with E.snapOut entry and E.launchIn exit; edgeMask for the faded edges; HardStep pushes for the discrete variant. Anatomy: Entry 81 px/f decaying to a 7.3 px/f cruise, exit to 31 px/f; discrete variant: pushes of 40-200 px per frame every 2-4 f. Sound: A whoosh on the exit.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Scroll`
- **Timing:** 100-160 f; chip swaps 35 f apart.
- **Use when:** Examples, creators, thumbnails, results.
- **Avoid when:** Constant speed.

### Chosen item enlarges while the rest dissolve

`dv-choose-one-dissolve` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · any

From a menu or a row of cards, the camera zooms into the chosen one (or it scales up 0.78 -> 1.0) while the others blur and fade into the background.

- **Build:** SnapZoom or Cards enterState on the chosen item; RackFocus levels on the rest. Anatomy: Chosen: expo-out scale or zoom; others: blur and fade over 14-16 f. Sound: A kick or a beat on the choice.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Timing:** Zoom 32-40 f; others 14-16 f.
- **Use when:** Selecting a product, a plan, a result.
- **Avoid when:** Keeping the others sharp.

### Container morph into its next role

`ui-container-morph` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

One element changes shape into what it becomes, a button unfolding into a panel, a card stretching into a detail view, a pill collapsing into an app tile, so there is no navigation cut to explain.

- **Build:** Keep one element mounted and animate its position (x and y inside one transform), width, height and border radius from the old rect to the new role's rect; never swap two elements. Use E.whip over 30-36 f (slow first 5 f, speed peak near 40%, long settle) and lengthen it so the fastest edge stays under about 70 px/f (frames >= 3.8 x edge travel / 70); a pill collapsing to a tile keeps its height locked while its radius goes from 999 px to 22% of its side, and a panel's radius eases from 44 to 36 px. The old content fades out in the first 12 f on E.smooth, a title that survives FLIPs to its header position and scale (1 to 0.6) on the same curve, flying at opacity 1 - 0.45*clamp((v - 20)/30) (v its speed in px/f) whenever it passes 20 px/f so it lands sharp, the new content enters 8 f after the speed peak with a 2-4 f stagger, and a backdrop behind a panel morph dims linearly over the same frames. Optional preface: the card's outline retracts first (SVG rect with pathLength 1, strokeDashoffset 0 to 1 over 15 f); for a content swap inside a card that stays, the old child leaves with depart() and blurOut(q, 8) over 18 f on E.in, the card resizes to the new aspect over 20 f on E.out, and the new child arrives with arrive() and blurIn(p, 8) over 18 f on E.out.
- **Primitive:** `fx/MorphChain.MorphChain`
- **Timing:** Morph 30-36 f (E.whip), edges <= 70 px/f. Old content out 12 f (E.smooth); title FLIP to 0.6 scale; new content +8 f after the peak, 2-4 f stagger; backdrop dim linear over the morph. Outline retract 15 f. Content swap: out 18 f (E.in), resize 20 f (E.out), in 18 f (E.out).
- **Use when:** A click that opens something (button to panel, card to detail), a status becoming an icon, an object docking into its slot.
- **Avoid when:** The size change comes from content or a drag (live reflow), or the two states have no visual relation.

### Container resizes, content reflows

`ui-live-reflow` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch

A card or window changes size because its content or the user changes it, growing as typed text wraps or narrowing as an edge is dragged, while everything inside reflows to the new width.

- **Build:** Make layout a pure function of the container's current width: measure text with measureTracked or inkBox, derive line breaks and block positions from that width, and evaluate typed text on fd(f) so the substring and the line count change on whole frames only. Content-driven: as the prompt starts, the input card widens from 67% to 77% of frame width over 24 f on E.outSoft (about 18 px/f per edge, centred so both edges move), and each newly wrapped line adds one line height over 12 f on E.out. User-driven: the cursor grabs a window's right edge and drags it 300-400 px inward on E.contact over 40 f, stopping dead like a real release with no settle, while the left edge follows at 15% of the right edge's speed so the window re-centres and the cursor trails the edge by 1 f. When the width crosses a breakpoint, compute both layouts and FLIP every block to its new slot over 16-24 f on E.ui (fastest block under 70 px/f) instead of crossfading the two layouts.
- **Timing:** Widen 67% to 77% FW over 24 f (E.outSoft); +1 line per wrap over 12 f (E.out). Drag 300-400 px over 40 f (E.contact), ends near 40 px/f, hard stop; breakpoint FLIP 16-24 f (E.ui); then a 0.3 px/f push-out.
- **Use when:** Typing into an input, responsive layouts, resizable panels: any moment where the point is that the UI adapts.
- **Avoid when:** The size change is a change of role, such as a button becoming a panel (use a container morph), or text must be read during the resize.

### Drag to reorder, siblings make way

`ui-drag-reorder-makeway` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy calm · walkthrough, feature

An item lifts under the cursor, travels on a slight arc to a new position while its neighbours slide aside one slot at a time, and settles into place with a firm landing and no bounce.

- **Build:** On the press (pressAt(f, grab)) the item moves to its own top layer and lifts: scale 1 to 1.03 and its shadow from 0 6px 16px at 8% to 0 18px 40px at 14% over 8 f on E.ui. It then follows cursorArc(from, to, prog(f, a, a + T, E.glide), 0.15) with T = max(36, 0.15 x distance) f, so it never exceeds 20 px/f and its label stays readable, and rotateZ = -0.15 deg per px/f of horizontal speed, clamped to +-4 deg. Siblings take their y from the computed layout for the currently hovered index, evaluated on fd(f), so each time that index changes the displaced sibling moves one pitch over 12 f on E.ui. On release the item settles into its slot with spr(f, drop, SPR.firm), the lift reverses over 10 f, its marker flashes C.accent and relaxes to neutral over 24 f, and a tick lands on the drop frame.
- **Timing:** Lift 8 f (E.ui), scale 1.03. Drag T = max(36, 0.15 x distance) f (E.glide) on a 0.15 bow, <= 20 px/f, tilt <= 4 deg. Sibling shift 12 f (E.ui) per index change. Drop SPR.firm, shadow back over 10 f, accent relax 24 f.
- **Use when:** Prioritising, scheduling, kanban boards, playlists: any product whose smart part is ordering things.
- **Avoid when:** The reorder is automatic (animate the computed reorder on one curve, with no cursor), or more than 2-3 drags would fall in one shot.

### Flick scroll: ramp, peak, friction

`dv-flick-scroll` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy high · any

Content accelerates by a constant ratio a frame into a peak, brakes on friction and lands; an exit whip can hand straight into the scroll; a column of cards decays from 68 px/f to a 2 px/f drift; the input bar decelerates into place as the conversation stops.

- **Build:** flickState({ ramp, peak, brake, distance }); declares the fast frames as a camera-blur range. Anatomy: Ramp x1.05-1.1 a frame to 176 px/f, friction x0.955 a frame (or x0.77 -> 0.85), brake time constant 0.73 s. Sound: A sub-bass drop on the peak speed; a stab on the landing.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Scroll`
- **Timing:** Exit 20 f; scroll 70-250 f.
- **Use when:** Feeds, lists, long conversations.
- **Avoid when:** Even-speed scrolling.

### Grid assembles cell by cell

`dv-grid-assemble` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · any

Outlined cards with logos slide into a grid with irregular stagger (one card snapping 880 px in a single frame); grid cells fill with blank tiles, then their text lines and progress bars fill in; rows of squares are born below and the block re-centres every frame.

- **Build:** Cards enterState per cell with seeded delays; HardStep for the snapping card. Anatomy: Stagger 1-8 f; slides 24 f; one-frame snap; blank card 3-4 f then content 4-8 f; squares grow 33 -> 82 px. Sound: Bubble pops; a pop per row.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Timing:** 28-74 f; rows every 2 f.
- **Use when:** Integrations, sponsors, a dashboard filling up.
- **Avoid when:** Perfectly even stagger.

### Inner UI pops in, left to right or top to bottom

`dv-inner-ui-cascade` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy calm · any

Inside a panel that has landed, chips, cards, a stat ring and buttons pop in with a 2 f stagger; agent log rows fade in one by one while the list scrolls; or the card stays and its content changes (the title retypes, the subtitle soft-reveals, the footer blurs away).

- **Build:** Cards / kit parts with starts every 4 f; TypeOn for the retype; Wipe gradient for the soft reveal. Anatomy: Stagger 2-5 f, short fades; a retype at 5-6 chars/f. Sound: UI ticks. Materials: Window chrome fills in item by item after the window lands: icon, then its label 6 f later (fade 4-6 f), header label 8 f after the landing, a chevron dropping 14 px in 6 f, a menu icon 10 f later; a footer row of icons pops in three stages over 8 f.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Materials:** Window chrome fills in item by item after the window lands: icon, then its label 6 f later (fade 4-6 f), header label 8 f after the landing, a chevron dropping 14 px in 6 f, a menu icon 10 f later; a footer row of icons pops in three stages over 8 f.
- **Timing:** 24 f for a panel; rows 6-10 f apart.
- **Use when:** Filling a panel after it lands.
- **Avoid when:** Filling before the panel has settled.

### Lens list scroll

`ui-lens-list-scroll` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, loop, vertical · also `dv-focus-band-list`

A list scrolls with momentum past an invisible lens line, and each item's size, tint or tilt depends on its distance from that line, like a phone picker, a rolodex cylinder or a smile-shaped arc.

- **Build:** Drive one offset s(f) for the whole list: a flicked picker uses s = D*(1 - (1 - p)^4) with p = prog(f, a, a + 120, E.linear) and D about 900 px (30 px/f at the start, under 20 px/f after 15 f, cut while it still drifts near 2 px/f, or land on an option with spr(f, a, SPR.detent)); a rolodex uses E.inOut over 90 f for about 480 px (peak about 41 px/f). Per item compute d, its distance from the lens line along the path, and map it: flat picker, scale = 1.2 - 0.35*min(|d|/375, 1) with text colour mixColor(C.ink, C.mute, min(|d|/375, 1)); cylinder, theta = d/R with R = 1.4*H, rotateX(theta) and translateZ(-(1 - cos theta)*R) under perspective 1600 px; smile arc, x = cx + R*sin(theta), y = cy + R*cos(theta) and rotate(-theta) with R = 1750 px and the centre about 790 px above the frame. Give each card a soft shadow; the depth comes from the geometry, never from translucent panels.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Scroll.Scroll`, `fx/Reels.FocusBand`
- **Timing:** Picker: 120 f quartic momentum, D ~900 px, 30 px/f start, < 20 px/f from f15, ~2 px/f at the cut; focus scale 1.2 to 0.85 across 375 px; optional SPR.detent landing. Cylinder: 90 f (E.inOut), ~480 px, peak ~41 px/f, R = 1.4H, perspective 1600 px. Arc: R 1750 px.
- **Use when:** Choosing among options, showing many screens as one continuous surface, or a playful list of choices that read one at a time.
- **Avoid when:** Items must be read while moving fast, or a plain scroll says it more simply.

### New item pushes in, older items step back

`dv-stack-push-demote` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · any

A new toast or card takes the top slot and the older ones step down, shrink and blur in depth; new rows push a list up with a snap scroll (75 % in the first frame); a queue keeps three and fades the oldest; new pills enter tilted and demote the older ones.

- **Build:** Cards cardArrive + demote (at = the newcomer's first frame). Anatomy: Per entry 22 f; older items scale 0.82-0.9 and blur one level; stagger 8-16 f (shortening 18 -> 10 f in a run); the stack can accelerate up into the next shot. Sound: A bell, then dings per toast; kicks within 40 ms.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Timing:** Entries 22 f; snap scroll 10-22 f; cards on kicks 26, 15, 18 f apart.
- **Use when:** Notifications, payments, steps of an agent, feature pills.
- **Avoid when:** Older items that stay at full strength.

### Panel arrives front-loaded on a tilted plane

`ui-front-loaded-panel` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · launch, update, feature, walkthrough · also `dv-panel-rise-front-loaded`

A product panel lands with its biggest step on the first frame and a long settle, riding a plane that is tilted back and flattens a few frames behind the position, so it arrives like an object, not a fade.

- **Build:** <Card frame={f} box={box} enter={{ start, dur, from: { y }, lean: { from: 10, to: 0, lag: 6 } }}> with the panel's UI as children (or a supplied screenshot as image). enterState() gives the numbers for anything that rides the panel. Optional defocus: { sigma: 4, frames: 6 } on the first frames, drawn as fixed-radius copies.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards.enterState`, `fx/Cards.Card`
- **Timing:** 34 f on E.snapOut (16-122 f), from 240 px below at 1080p; the first frame carries 22-50 % of the travel. Lean 10 deg flattening on E.glideOut, 6 f behind the position.
- **Use when:** The first appearance of the product, a new screen, a panel that carries the next feature.
- **Avoid when:** Small chips and badges (use a press or a cut-on instead).

### Push-aside with bound layout

`ui-push-aside-reflow` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

An incoming panel or card enters from the edge and the neighbouring content moves aside because it is bound to the panel's edge, so one motion moves two elements and nothing overlaps.

- **Build:** Bind instead of tweening twice: each frame set neighbour.x = min(restX, panel.left - gap), so the neighbour reflows from the panel's own position. Shove: a dark card (C.ink2, radius 24 px, about 62% of frame width) enters from beyond the right edge over 72 f on E.whip (peak about 72 px/f at 40% under the motion-blur pass) and is placed so it reaches the headline word only after 58% of its move, where the card has slowed to 20 px/f or less, so the shoved word stays readable. Make room: a side panel 36% of frame width slides in on E.glide over 54 f (peak about 38 px/f) while the content card moves 0.43x the panel's travel on E.smooth, starting 28 f before the panel so it anticipates the arrival; the exit mirrors both over about 50 f. For copy, the product card glides 370 px aside and scales 1 to 0.83 on E.glide over 48 f (peak about 23 px/f) while the headline rises line by line into the freed side (Words, 6 f stagger), starting 4-6 f after the slide.
- **Timing:** Shove: 72 f (E.whip), contact after 58% of the move, word <= 20 px/f. Side panel: 36% FW over 54 f (E.glide); neighbour 0.43x travel with a 28 f lead (E.smooth); exit ~50 f. Copy: 370 px + scale 0.83 over 48 f (E.glide); lines 6 f apart from +4-6 f.
- **Use when:** Introducing a detail panel, a new card or a caption beside existing UI, or a joke where the layout itself does the gag.
- **Avoid when:** The incoming element should float above (modal, popover), or there is no room to move into.

### Row cascade

`ui-row-cascade` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · any

List rows or cards appear one after another from top to bottom, each rising a few pixels as it fades in, so the list reads as data streaming in.

- **Build:** For row i, start = t0 + 4*i (6*i for taller cards); translateY 8 to 0 px through arrive() and opacity 0 to 1, both over 12 f on E.out, placed by transform only. When two columns describe input and output, give both sides the same row index so the build is mirrored and 5 rows complete in about 30 f. Let each row's text land in C.mute and darken to C.ink over 12 f, 40 f after the row arrives (mixColor), so the eye reads the structure first and the words second. Start the cascade about 20 f before the previous move (a transition, a portal edge) finishes, so the start of the scene is hidden inside it.
- **Timing:** Stagger 4 f (rows) to 6 f (cards); each row 12 f (E.out), 6-12 px rise; ink-in 12 f at +40 f; overlap the previous move by ~20 f.
- **Use when:** Populating any list, inbox, table, feed or a pair of mirrored input and output columns.
- **Avoid when:** Rows are added one at a time over a longer beat (top insert), or the list arrives by scrolling (flick scroll).

### Shell first, then contents, then the action

`ui-shell-first-build` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough, vertical

The empty container is on screen first, its contents arrive left to right, the card unfolds downward in stages, and the primary button fills last as the clear call to act.

- **Build:** Show the container (bar, card, window) at t0 with nothing inside; its children enter in DOM order at a 4 f stagger, each rising 6 px through arrive() with opacity 0 to 1 over 12 f on E.out, and media slots first appear as C.mist rounded rects that fill with their image over 8 f, 8 f apart. The primary action comes last: its background ramps from transparent to solid on E.linear over 16 f from +20 f, and its label colour inverts on a single frame at +28 f. To teach the hierarchy, unfold the card downward in stages with a clip-path inset on its bottom edge on E.smooth (header row first, then 36 f to reveal the stats row, then 24 f to the full card, the bottom edge travelling about 330 px), each stage's content starting only once its slot is 60% revealed. Headlines inside the UI are live text in the camera world, revealed per word with Words (6 f stagger), so they inherit the plane's perspective.
- **Timing:** Children 4 f stagger, 12 f each (E.out), 6 px rise. Media fill 8 f, 8 f apart. Button fill 16 f (E.linear) from +20 f; label inverts at +28 f. Unfold 36 f then 24 f (E.smooth), content at 60% open. In-UI headline 6 f per word.
- **Use when:** The first appearance of any real product screen, especially dashboards, headers and forms whose reading order matters.
- **Avoid when:** The screen should feel already alive on the cut (enter it moving with a rise-in), or the shot is shorter than about 40 f.

### Spawn from the anchor point

`ui-anchor-point-spawn` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · walkthrough, feature, launch

Menus, popovers, drop targets and detail cards scale out of the exact point that caused them, such as the cursor tip or a map pin, and collapse back into it.

- **Build:** Set transform-origin to the trigger point in the element's own coordinates (cursor tip, pin base, the edge of the button) and scale with lmix from about 0.05, opacity reaching 1 within the first 4 f; the log-space scale keeps the far edge from jumping on frame 1. Small surfaces (menus, popovers, a card out of a pin): lmix(0.05, 1, prog(f, a, a + 12, E.out)), no overshoot, adding 2 f per extra 100 px of size, then a small camera reframe toward the surface starting 2 f later over 20-40 f on E.cam. Large surfaces (a drop target filling a panel): lmix(0.036, 1, prog(f, a, a + 48, E.smooth)), a flat C.accent fill with a 12 px radius, its icon and hint text fading in over the last 8 f; it collapses back into the point over 36 f on E.smooth. Keep the cursor (fx/Cursor.tsx) parked on the trigger during the spawn so cause and effect share one point.
- **Timing:** Small: 12 f (lmix, E.out) from 0.05, opacity 4 f, far edge ~63 px/f for a 300 px menu; camera reframe from +2 f over 20-40 f (E.cam). Large: 48 f (lmix, E.smooth) from 0.036, hint over the last 8 f, collapse 36 f (E.smooth).
- **Use when:** Any UI that opens from a click, or a drag target appearing: menus, popovers, dialogs, drop zones, cards from a map pin.
- **Avoid when:** The element enters from off-screen or is a full window (rise-in), or the trigger point is out of frame.

### Tile slides out to clear a slot for the next actor

`dv-clear-the-slot` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · any

A tile slides out on an in-out curve leaving a stub, and the next actor (a cursor, a tile) enters the vacated space 2 f before it settles; a secondary tile shift overlaps the previous move by 11 f.

- **Build:** Cards enterState out on E.strongInOut; the next actor starting 4 f before the end. Anatomy: Quart in-out, peak 91-117 px/f, no blur; overlap 11 f. Sound: None.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Timing:** 30-34 f.
- **Use when:** Making space inside a bento or layout for a demo action.
- **Avoid when:** Moves that end before the next one starts (overlap them).

### Top insert pushes the list down

`ui-top-insert-push` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, loop, walkthrough

New items arrive at the top of a list one at a time and every earlier item slides down one slot, on a steady metronome that reads as abundance or on a slower cadence where each row resolves as it is generated.

- **Build:** Compute every item's y from the data each frame (listLayout from the product-ui reference, newest at index 0), so earlier items slide down one pitch on E.ui as each new one mounts; overlapping pushes simply add. Metronome: one insert every 14 f with a 155 px pitch pushed over 20 f (about 21 px/f); the new pill reveals left to right with clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) to inset(0) over 12 f on E.ui, its icon leading and its label fading in 4 f later, while any paired object (an item landing on a stack) drops 60-90 px with opacity over 10 f on E.out; wrap the group in a camera drift whose velocity decays as vStart*0.97^f from about 19 to 3 px/f over 90 f. Generation: one insert every 36-40 f, the row starting at scaleX 0.6 about its left edge with blurIn(p, 6) and an 8% C.accent tint, reaching full width, sharp and neutral over 12 f on E.out while the rows below move 66 px over 10 f on E.ui. Put a tick on each insert frame (LANDINGS) so the cadence is heard.
- **Timing:** Metronome: every 14 f, push 155 px over 20 f (E.ui), pill reveal 12 f (E.ui), label +4 f, camera drift 19 to 3 px/f (x0.97 per frame). Generation: every 36-40 f, resolve 12 f (E.out) from scaleX 0.6 and 6 px blur, push 66 px over 10 f (E.ui).
- **Use when:** Results, messages, subtasks or saved items accumulating: generated rows, imports landing, a feed or a stack filling up.
- **Avoid when:** The whole list should appear at once (row cascade), or there are so many inserts that the pushes blur into noise (scroll instead).

### UI rises in, holds, launches out

`dv-rise-hold-launch` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · any

Each UI piece (input box, share sheet, composer, search field) rises 40-260 px into place, holds briefly, then accelerates up and out with a smear; a search field can whip in while the camera pulls back, type, and drift up.

- **Build:** Cards enterState + an exit on E.launchIn with a 2-frame vertical ghost. Anatomy: Rise expo-out, hold, ease-in exit with vertical smear; pull-back x0.65 quint-out. Sound: Whooshes on the exits; keypress ticks.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Timing:** Rise 22-32 f; exit 24-32 f; typing 38 f.
- **Use when:** A rapid sequence of UI moments.
- **Avoid when:** Fading out.

### Bubbles spring-pop from their tail corner

`dv-tail-anchored-bubble-pop` · ui choreography · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

Speech bubbles pop around a subject in a photo, each scaling up from its tail corner with a small spring, on the voice's cadence.

- **Build:** springBox per bubble with transformOrigin at the tail. Anatomy: Scale from the tail anchor; spring zeta 0.62; irregular gaps from the voice. Sound: Chat pops. Materials: Each bubble starts as a short white dash (20 x 3 px) exactly at its tail corner for 2 f, then a tiny squashed bubble springs out from the tail (spring about 8 f, damping 12) and settles in 6 f.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Materials:** Each bubble starts as a short white dash (20 x 3 px) exactly at its tail corner for 2 f, then a tiny squashed bubble springs out from the tail (spring about 8 f, damping 12) and settles in 6 f.
- **Timing:** Rise 12-14 f, settle 40 f; gaps 6-26 f.
- **Use when:** Questions or messages around a person in footage.
- **Avoid when:** Spending the spring elsewhere in the same film.

### Chips fall like objects and float back

`dv-chip-physics` · ui choreography · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

When the line says "disconnected", the chips around it fall like objects (accelerating), land in a cluster at the bottom and straighten as they land, then drift back up; after popping, chips can float upward on a very long tail.

- **Build:** Build: gravityDrop(f, { at, fall, rot, drift }) (fx/Flight): the fall on E.buildIn (24 f), the rotation flattening over the last 30 %, then a slow drift back up (2.5 px/f at 60). Anatomy: Fall 7 -> 67 px/f, rotation flattening on landing, drift back -5 px/f; float 220 px on a long expo-out still moving 3 px/f at the end. Sound: Camera-shutter clicks and bubble pops.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Flight`
- **Timing:** Fall 24 f; float 68 f (t90 1.13 s).
- **Use when:** Showing disorder or separation with UI chips.
- **Avoid when:** Bounces (land, do not bounce).

### Clutter pile-up, then strip to one

`ui-clutter-pileup-strip` · ui choreography · accent · energy high · launch, feature, vertical

Clicks spawn copies of a control until the frame is a messy pile, then elements vanish one per beat and the survivors snap to re-centre until a single tile remains.

- **Build:** Pile-up: on each click (pressAt from fx/Cursor.tsx) spawn a clone every 4 f for about 60 f at x = (rand(i) - 0.5)*500 and y = (rand(i + 99) - 0.5)*300 px, each travelling 40-80 px out from the previous clone over 8 f on E.out while scaling 0.9 to 1, so the motion-blur pass smears every spawn, and drift the whole pile up 1.5 px/f. Strip: hold the survivors in an array whose length drops at listed frames, one removal every 5-7 f, choose the state with fd(f), and compute the centred layout from the current array with no tween, so the remaining tiles jump to their new places on the removal frame. Hold the last survivor 17 f under a 0.5% scale drift (breath() from lib/camera.ts), then exit it or let it become the next shot. Put a soft tick on every spawn and removal, rising in level, so the acceleration is heard.
- **Timing:** Spawns every 4 f for ~60 f (12-15 clones), 8 f each (E.out, 40-80 px), pile drift 1.5 px/f. Removals every 5-7 f with an instant re-centre (fd); last survivor 17 f with a 0.5% drift.
- **Use when:** Showing overload (too many tools, buttons, tabs, notifications) and then focus: the product reduces chaos to the one thing that matters.
- **Avoid when:** Calm or premium films, or elements whose text must be read; the jumps are deliberately abrupt.

### Code types in plain ink; syntax colours arrive a few frames later

`dv-late-syntax-colour` · ui choreography · accent · energy calm · feature, update

A code snippet types line by line in plain dark monospace; a few frames after each token is complete its syntax colour switches on (placeholders and string values flip from ink to the accent), as if the editor were catching up.

- **Build:** Recipe: TypeOn over tokenised code; a token takes its colour once the frame is 10 f past its completion. Anatomy: Mono about 14 px at 1080p, line height 1.6; the colour about 10 f after the token completes; the accent only on placeholders and strings. Sound: Key ticks under the VO.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeFx.CodeType`
- **Timing:** About 55 f of typing for a short snippet; recolours staggered with the tokens.
- **Use when:** SDK, API and developer products; any code card.
- **Avoid when:** Fast walls of code, where the delay cannot be read.

### Genie launch from an icon

`ui-genie-launch-from-icon` · ui choreography · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

A dock or home-screen icon flares open at its top into a curved funnel that keeps widening until it fills the frame, and the app's first screen is already sitting inside it.

- **Build:** Render the app's first screen full-frame above the current scene and clip it with clip-path: path(), rebuilt every frame from a few numbers. The bottom edge sits on the icon's base with width wb; the top edge is h above it with width wt. Each side is a quadratic curve whose control point is the bottom corner raised by 0.45 h, so the outline pinches like a funnel. Grow it in log space so it leaves the icon slowly and speeds up: h = lmix(iconH, H + 120, p) and wt = lmix(iconW, W + 240, p), with p = prog(f, a, a + 44, E.linear). Over the same 44 f, the top edge's centre drifts from the icon to the frame centre on E.smooth, which peaks mid-way, before the growth gets fast. In the last 24 f, with s = prog(f, a + 20, a + 44, E.smooth), the waist widens toward the top (wb = mix(iconW, wt, s)) and the bottom edge drops from the icon base to 60 px below the frame. With these numbers the fastest edge stays near 70-75 px/f on the final frames, under the motion-blur pass. Start the funnel 4 f after pressAt on the icon (the icon's tile darkens 10% on the press frame). Either keep the revealed screen still at its final size, or let it settle from 1.04 to 1 over the same 44 f on E.outSoft. On the first frame the path covers the whole frame, unmount the clip and the old scene, and start the app's first UI event (a caret, a typed greeting) on that frame, so the launch hands straight over to the product.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Fill the funnel with the app's real first screen on its flat stage colour, or with one flat colour taken from the icon, never the icon's colour ramp. The clip path, the log-space growth and the timing stay the same. The full look relies on gradient; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Press, then funnel from +4 f: 44 f in log space (about x1.06-1.08 per frame, E.linear progress). Centre drift over the same 44 f (E.smooth). Waist and bottom edge open over the last 24 f (E.smooth). Fastest edge ~70-75 px/f at the end. Optional content settle 1.04 to 1 over 44 f (E.outSoft). Clip removed on full cover; the next UI event starts on that frame.
- **Use when:** Opening an app, a document or a tool from its icon in a dock, launcher or home screen, as a playful product-native scene change.
- **Avoid when:** The product is never launched from an icon, or the film already has a genie (once is a gag, twice reads as a template).

### Path fractures into a fan, then re-converges

`ui-path-fracture-fan` · ui choreography · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

A solid line draws out, breaks into dashes, splits into a fan of curves that end on obstacle pills, and later the curves funnel back into one point that becomes the next diagram.

- **Build:** Draw the trunk from the source node as an SVG path with pathLength 1, strokeDashoffset 1 to 0 on E.linear over 12 f; at +12 f let it degrade by tweening strokeDasharray from 'L 0' to '24 12' over 8 f (dash = mix(L, 24, p), gap = mix(0, 12, p)). At +26 f split it into 6 cubic beziers from one shared point with their ends spread +-200 px in y, each revealed by its own dashoffset on E.glide over 24 f at a 2 f stagger so the drawing head stays under about 70 px/f, and pop a labelled obstacle pill at each end as its curve arrives (opacity step plus scale 0.9 to 1 over 8 f on E.out). Hard-cut to a 2.5x punch-in on the pills about 10 f after the fan completes. To resolve, give each pill a trailing bezier ending on one point, the next diagram's first node, draw them over 24 f on E.smooth while the camera travels the same way with no cut, and finish the camera's travel with an E.out landing of about 210 px over 60 f (22 px/f at its start) through lib/camera.ts.
- **Timing:** Trunk 12 f (E.linear); dashes at +12 f over 8 f to '24 12'; fan at +26 f: 6 curves x 24 f (E.glide), 2 f stagger, complete at +60 f; punch-in cut at ~+70 f (2.5x). Converge 24 f (E.smooth); camera landing 210 px over 60 f (E.out), 22 px/f at its start.
- **Use when:** Explaining the friction of an old way (one simple path turning into many obstacles) before the turn to one clean path.
- **Avoid when:** The viewer needs real product UI on screen; this is diagram language, and a diagram act longer than about 4 s loses the thread.

### Stalled state by dimming

`ui-stalled-state` · ui choreography · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

A token stops on its rail, the destination greys out, short status words appear one after another, and the frame goes briefly still so the blockage is felt.

- **Build:** Split the rail at the stalled token: the travelled part solid, the part ahead dotted (strokeDasharray '2 4'), both drawn from the same path and clipped at the token's position. On the stall frame the destination node dims to 30% (opacity, or mixColor toward C.mute) over 8 f on E.smooth; status words then appear beside the token at +6, +28 and +40 f, each an opacity step with a 6 px rise through arrive() over 8 f on E.out, and at +51 f the first word dims to 40% so the decisive word (the reason, the day) stands alone. Bring the camera to zero velocity for a designed freeze of at most 15 f on a gap in the sound, then resume a 0.3 px/f drift so nothing sits static past 48 f.
- **Timing:** Node dim 8 f (E.smooth) to 30%. Status words at +6/+28/+40 f, 8 f each (E.out, 6 px rise); first word dims at +51 f. Freeze <= 15 f on a silence, then 0.3 px/f drift.
- **Use when:** The problem beat: money, a message or a task stuck waiting (closed, pending, rejected) just before the product unblocks it.
- **Avoid when:** The film has no problem act, or the block would sit longer than about 1.5 s; stillness only works as a short contrast to the motion around it.

### Tilted page sweeps up, develops colour, is scrolled

`dv-develop-sweep-page` · ui choreography · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

A white product page tilted in perspective sweeps up from the bottom in a few frames, its illustration develops from ghost grey through a tint to full colour, and the camera scrolls it in three moves.

- **Build:** Cards enterState (lean 20) + Develop + reframeChain. Anatomy: Sweep 12 f; develop grey -> tint -> colour; three scroll moves. Sound: A spoken word, then a punchy hit.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Develop`
- **Timing:** 256 f in all.
- **Use when:** A product page or a landing page shown as an object.
- **Avoid when:** Flat, untilted pages (they read as screenshots).

### Avatar bubbles swoop, orbit and split

`dv-avatar-bubble-choreo` · ui choreography · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

Round avatar bubbles behave like characters: one swoops in on an arc from an impact point and drifts; two orbit around their midpoint and swap sides while one splits into a group; a smaller bubble is ejected from a group bubble on an arc and grows.

- **Build:** Recipe: polar paths in closed form (angle on an ease, radius on its own curve); the split is a MorphChain swap at mid-orbit. Anatomy: Arc paths (peak 137 px/f), orbit 154 deg (peak 13.4 deg/f), growth +30 % mid-swap, ejection r 87 -> 164 px in 8 f. Sound: A UI pop on arrival; voice. Materials: A bubble first appears as an empty glass ring (rim 4-6 px, a gradient from the tint to white, an inner radial gradient from a white centre to the tint at the edge, a specular dot low right), then its glyph rises from the lower edge into place clipped by the ring (8-10 f, expo-out); the next bubble repeats it 18 f later.
- **Materials:** A bubble first appears as an empty glass ring (rim 4-6 px, a gradient from the tint to white, an inner radial gradient from a white centre to the tint at the edge, a specular dot low right), then its glyph rises from the lower edge into place clipped by the ring (8-10 f, expo-out); the next bubble repeats it 18 f later.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** Swoop 75-85 f; orbit 90 f; ejection 20 f.
- **Use when:** Collaboration and people features.
- **Avoid when:** More than three bubbles.

### Cards fly in radially on one ease

`dv-radial-card-swarm` · ui choreography · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

Seven small tilted UI cards (lists, notes, charts, messages) fly in radially from off-screen on one shared exponential ease and settle around the centre, their rotation tails running long.

- **Build:** Cards cardArrive per card on one curve with radial from vectors and rot 8-35 deg. Anatomy: Shared curve, per-card direction and tilt; rotation settles last. Sound: Voice.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Timing:** Each visible 28-48 f; rotation tail 120 f.
- **Use when:** Showing many parts of a product at once around a statement.
- **Avoid when:** Cards with readable detail (they are too small to read).

### Fanned stack resolves into slots

`ui-fan-resolve-to-slots` · ui choreography · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, vertical

A tilted, overlapping stack of cards spreads into an even row, or each card flips to show its face and flies small into a slot of a list grid where its label resolves.

- **Build:** Start with 4-6 cards stacked 20 px apart with seeded tilts (rand(i) mapped to +-6 deg), or a fan (rotateZ -20 deg, rotateY 25 deg, 40 px offset), z-order from the stack. Row preset: x = mix(stackX + 20*i, slotX_i, p) and rotate = mix(seed_i, 0, p) with p = prog(f, t0 + 2*i, t0 + 2*i + T, E.out) and T = max(24, 0.09 x travel) f, so the farthest card stays under 70 px/f and nothing overshoots. Flip preset: card i starts at t0 + 6*i, turns rotateY 0 to 180 deg on E.linear over 6 f, or 8 f for cards wider than 200 px so the edge stays near 50 px/f at edge-on (swapping from its muted back to its full face at 90 deg), drifts on E.out for 12 f (28 down to 7 px/f), then FLIPs to its grid slot rect (scale about 0.25, rotateZ to 0) over max(12, travel/20) f on E.rest; its label then rises 6 px and clears from blurIn(p, 6) over 8 f. Six cards should land within about 60 f.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards.cardArrive`
- **Timing:** Row: 2 f stagger, T = max(24, 0.09 x travel) f (E.out), tilt +-6 deg. Flip: 6 f stagger, flip 6 f (8 f over 200 px wide, E.linear), drift 12 f (E.out), FLIP to slot max(12, travel/20) f (E.rest), label 8 f; six cards in ~60 f.
- **Use when:** Many options, offers, integrations or tools becoming an orderly set: the 'all in one place' or 'compare them all' beat.
- **Avoid when:** The cards must be read while they move, or there is only one card.

### Orbit gather and merge

`ui-orbit-gather-merge` · ui choreography · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, loop

Tokens swing into orbit around a node, slow to a lazy spin, then accelerate one by one into a single exit point from which a line shoots out.

- **Build:** Place 4 tokens on a 95 px radius around the source node (above the node, below the exit line) and drive each angle in closed form: theta_i(f) = theta0 + 90*i - (132.5*(1 - exp(-f/10)) + 2*f) deg, a 13 deg/f swing (about 22 px/f of arc) that decays to a 2 deg/f spin within 30 f. Token 0 is there at f0; tokens 1-3 spawn at f10, f18 and f28, each scaling 0 to 1 over 10 f on E.out. Pick theta0 so each token is 90-120 deg short of the exit angle (3 o'clock) when its merge starts; token i then covers that remaining angle forward over 16 f on E.contact, landing at f72, f82 and f86 at under 60 px/f, its scale cutting to 0 on arrival while the exit node takes scale 1 + 0.08*hitPulse(t) and a tick. At f92 a line draws out of the exit point (pathLength 1, strokeDashoffset 1 to 0 over 12 f on E.out) and carries the story to the next diagram.
- **Timing:** omega = 13.25*exp(-f/10) + 2 deg/f, radius 95 px at 1080p. Spawns f10/f18/f28, 10 f each (E.out). Merges 16 f each (E.contact), landing f72/f82/f86 at < 60 px/f; hitPulse(t, 2, 5) on the exit node. Exit line f92, 12 f (E.out). About 105 f in all.
- **Use when:** Several inputs, funds or sources gather before one action (pooling, batching, syncing, sending) and the idea should be told by physics with no words.
- **Avoid when:** The tokens are UI cards carrying text (unreadable while orbiting), or the story has no single output point.

### Outline-led insert and spawn

`ui-outline-led-reveal` · ui choreography · signature · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch

A thin accent line or a heavy outline appears first and opens into a new row or a modal, then the stroke decays to a hairline so the content takes over.

- **Build:** Row insert: a 2 px C.accent line appears across the list in one frame at the insert position, then the row opens from height 0 to row height over 10 f on E.ui, pushing the rows below through the computed list layout at 20 px/f or less; its 2 px border decays from the accent to 40% over 24 f on E.linear and then to nothing, and the row's content fades in over the last 4 f of the open. Repeat inserts every 41 f so three new rows read as a countable rhythm, each with a tick on its line frame. Modal spawn: the modal scales lmix(0.07, 1, prog(f, a, a + 26, E.out)) about the trigger point while an overlay stroke in the accent runs 6 to 10 to 1 px wide (interpolate(p, [0, 0.6, 1], [6, 10, 1]) on the same progress); after landing it thins to 1 px over 12 f and its opacity falls to 0.3, leaving a clean modal. At its peak the stroke can carry a faint outer glow, which the hard bans rule out; build it flat (see the variant).
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Use a flat 2 px stroke in the film's single accent with no box-shadow, bloom or blur; express the flash as stroke width (2 to 3 px for 4 f via hitPulse) and an opacity decay from 1 to 0.4 to 0 over 24 f, and frame the modal with a solid 6-10 px accent stroke that thins to 1 px. The full look relies on glow; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Line 1 f; open 10 f (E.ui); border decay 24 f (E.linear); content in the last 4 f; inserts every 41 f. Modal 26 f (lmix on E.out) from scale 0.07, far edge ~52 px/f; stroke 6/10/1 px; thin 12 f; opacity to 0.3.
- **Use when:** A click that creates something (a new account, row, record or dialog) that must read from a wide shot, or repeated creation shown as a rhythm.
- **Avoid when:** The accent already means something else in the film, or the shot is a calm monochrome close-up where a bright stroke would shout.

### Resize: small creep, one big jump, long settle

`dv-resize-creep-jump` · ui choreography · signature · energy high · launch, feature

A card or field is resized the way a tool resizes it: a short anticipation creep, one big jump frame (50-70 % of the change) with stretched echo handles, then a long settle; an emptied field stretches with a slow-in, a 3-frame lunge and a long tail while the caret glides.

- **Build:** Build: <ResizeBox at from to handle line radius>{content}</ResizeBox> (fx/Resize): creep 15 % over 12 f (E.softIn), ONE jump frame of 60 % with the corner handles stretched back as echo bars, then an exponential settle (24 f); jumpFrames={3} is the field version (a three-frame lunge). Anatomy: Creep under 20 % over 4-6 f; jump 1 f; settle 8-10 f; handles stretch toward the new edge on the jump frame and snap back. Sound: The jump on a snare (+5 ms); a kick on the lunge.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Resize.ResizeBox`
- **Timing:** 43-90 f; field lunge peak 66 px/f.
- **Use when:** Editing, resizing, aspect changes, expanding a field.
- **Avoid when:** Smooth tweens for a tool action.

### Toss into a bin with one rebound

`ui-discard-into-bin` · ui choreography · signature · energy high · launch, feature, vertical

Icons or chips are thrown into a container that rises in to catch them, drop through its mouth and peek back out once before settling.

- **Build:** Layer order, back to front: bin body, thrown items, bin front lip, with the items clipped by a clipPath at the mouth so they vanish inside; the bin rises 160 px on E.out over 24 f. Toss: each item rises about 260 px on E.out over 24 f (about 68 px/f on its first frame), hangs 3 f, then falls about 340 px on E.contact over 22 f while rotateZ goes to +-15 deg (sign from rand(i)) and x eases to the mouth on E.smooth, entering at no more than 70 px/f under the motion-blur pass. Chain variant: chips follow an SVG path into the bin, chip i at path.getPointAtLength(L*E.contact(prog(f, t0 + 5*i, t0 + 5*i + 60, E.linear))) rotated to the tangent (atan2 of a 1 px look-ahead), the element they trail squashed to a 6 px tall tail. Six frames after the last entry the contents peek back up about 24 px on spr(f, hit, SPR.land) and settle within 16 f, the rim takes squash(t), and a low 60 to 30 Hz thud lands on that frame; this counts as one of the film's two spring landings.
- **Timing:** Bin rise 160 px, 24 f (E.out). Item rise ~260 px, 24 f (E.out); hang 3 f; fall ~340 px, 22 f (E.contact), <= 70 px/f; tilt +-15 deg. Chain: 60 f per chip (E.contact along the path), 5 f lag. Rebound at +6 f, ~24 px, SPR.land, settled in 16 f.
- **Use when:** A comic or decisive 'throw the old way away' beat: replacing old tools, clearing clutter, deleting the problem.
- **Avoid when:** Serious, calm or enterprise tone, or the film has already used its two spring landings.

### Chat bubbles cut on and slide home

`ui-chat-bubbles` · product demo · workhorse · energy medium · launch, update, feature, vertical · also `dv-chat-bubble-slide`

Each message cuts on at full size below its slot and slides up on an exponential while the conversation lifts a little to make room; replies come a beat later, a typing bubble pulses until the answer replaces it.

- **Build:** <Bubbles frame={f} messages={[{ text, side, at }, { kind: 'typing', ... }]} role='caption' lift={{ share: 0.25, tau: 4 }} header={avatar} />. bubbleY / bubbleState / bubbleFrames give the numbers and the sound cue frames.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Bubbles`
- **Timing:** tau 12 f (10-16), home at 50 f, travel 56 px at 1080p (38-70), reply 32 f later (20-32).
- **Use when:** An assistant, a team thread, a support conversation, a message composer.
- **Avoid when:** More than four bubbles in one beat; text below the caption role on screen.

### Flick scroll lands the target

`pd-flick-scroll-lands-target` · product demo · workhorse · energy medium · any

A list scrolls like a trackpad flick: speed builds by a constant ratio a frame, peaks, brakes on friction in two stages and lands the target row at its reading position; the fast frames render with camera blur.

- **Build:** <Scroll frame={f} start={at} distance={targetY - restY} width height edge={40}>{rows}</Scroll>; flickState() gives y and speed; copy declares(props) into the timeline's CAMERA_BLUR so the blur pass renders the fast frames with the shutter in a crisp film. lead starts it while an earlier move is still carrying speed.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Scroll.flickState`
- **Timing:** Ramp x1.05 a frame for 66 f to 2600 px/s at 1080p, hold 6 f, brake x0.82 for 40 % of the speed then coast x0.977 a frame; blur above 900 px/s.
- **Use when:** Showing volume (many results, a long page, a feed), or moving down a form to its next section with a human feel.
- **Avoid when:** The viewer must read during the move; the list is shorter than two screens; it would be the third scroll in a row.

### Phone demo: pull back, tilt while scrolling, press, popup

`dv-phone-tilt-scroll-demo` · product demo · workhorse · energy medium · feature, walkthrough

Close on the app header, pull back; the phone tilts away in 3D while its content scrolls with in-out gestures; a cursor clicks, a floating button presses, a popup grows from its anchor.

- **Build:** camera pull + Cards lean + Scroll + press + springBox from the anchor. Anatomy: Pull 26 f; scroll 70 f; press 6-8 f; popup 16 f from the anchor. Sound: UI clicks.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Timing:** About 190 f.
- **Use when:** Mobile app walkthroughs.
- **Avoid when:** Straight-on flat phones for the whole demo.

### Thumbnails stay alive inside the cards

`dv-live-thumbnails` · product demo · workhorse · energy calm · any

Cards contain playing motion pieces: logo marks swap colour, words morph, images move, so a board of cards is never a still screenshot.

- **Build:** Recipe: each card renders a small composition in <Loop> with awkward periods. Anatomy: Per card a tiny loop with its own period. Sound: None.
- **Timing:** Continuous; letter swaps 14 f.
- **Use when:** Boards, galleries, dashboards with media.
- **Avoid when:** Every thumbnail moving at once at full speed.

### Button flies in carrying the pointer

`dv-cta-flies-in-pointer` · product demo · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

A call-to-action button enters bottom-right tilted and small, travels on a curved path carrying the pointer with it, and takes a word's slot in the line.

- **Build:** cursorMove on a bowed path with the button attached to the cursor's transform. Anatomy: Start -7 deg at 80 % size; x peak 147 px/f before y peak 32 px/f (curved path). Sound: A pop and whoosh.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cursor`
- **Timing:** 36 f.
- **Use when:** Ending a demo on the action.
- **Avoid when:** Pointer and button on separate paths.

### Code streams in line by line

`dv-code-stream-lines` · product demo · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

Code lines appear in a panel about one line every 2 frames, stepped, carrying the only saturated colours in the frame (syntax colours), and keep streaming under a zoom-out.

- **Build:** TypeOn kind="stream" with a line-quantised count. Anatomy: One line per 2 f; syntax colours as the only saturation. Sound: None distinct.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeOn`
- **Timing:** 46 f.
- **Use when:** Developer products; "it writes the code".
- **Avoid when:** Readable fake code (keep it plausible, real-looking).

### Panels shrink away and seeds build the logo

`dv-panels-to-logo` · logo and end card · signature · energy medium · launch

Large blank panels shrink into one corner while coloured seed squares scatter and fly to build the logo in the opposite corner, and the words land in the accent: "one place".

- **Build:** Cards demote toward a corner + Wordmark assemble with parts starting from the panels' centres. Anatomy: Panels shrink to the corner; seeds fly on arcs; words 2 f apart. Sound: A ding.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Wordmark`
- **Timing:** 34 f; glyphs 1-2 f.
- **Use when:** Consolidation claims; the move from product to brand.
- **Avoid when:** Logos without separable parts.

### Bento cell takes over the frame

`lc-bento-cell-takeover` · layout and composition · signature · energy high · loop, launch, feature

In a flush four-cell grid, one cell grows to fill the whole frame while its siblings are pushed off the edges, still playing as they go, turning a breadth overview into one focused shot without a cut.

- **Build:** Build a flush 2x2 grid as in oh-live-grid-cold-open: gap 0, cells exactly W/2 x H/2 on whole pixels, overflow hidden and C.ink in every cell so the seams vanish, with every cell's scene rendered at full 1920x1080 inside a wrapper with scale(0.5) and transformOrigin '0 0'. Scale the whole grid container from 1 to 2 with lmix on prog(f, a, a + 64, E.smooth), about the chosen cell's outer corner (transformOrigin '0 0' for the top-left cell, '100% 100%' for the bottom-right). That corner stays fixed, the chosen cell lands exactly on the frame at native resolution, and the other cells slide out of frame. Keep every cell's loop running through the move and apply motion blur while the far edge exceeds 12 px/f; on landing, drop the grid and continue the cell's scene as a normal shot.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards.Bento`
- **Timing:** 64 f on E.smooth; content at the far frame edge peaks around 60 px/f (the far corner about 68 px/f), with motion blur. Cells keep playing throughout. Follow with at least 90 f of the full-frame scene. To return to the overview, run it in reverse (scale 2 to 1, 64 f, E.smooth).
- **Use when:** A loop or launch that opens on four-up breadth and then dives into one feature; returning to the overview between features.
- **Avoid when:** A chosen cell whose scene was not composed for full frame (it will look sparse), or more than twice per film.

### Bento unfolds on one shared curve

`ui-bento-unfold` · layout and composition · signature · energy high · launch, update, feature · also `dv-bento-unfold`

One layout opens into the next: every tile travels from its old box to its new one (position, size, radius, fill) on the same front-loaded curve, the main tiles together and the edges a few frames later; content keeps its size and is revealed by the moving boxes, pictures re-crop as their boxes grow.

- **Build:** <Bento frame={f} tiles={[{ A, B, content | image }]} start={at} delays={[0, 0, 2, 8, 18]} />. Lay A out as the state before (thumbnails in a panel, a row of chips) and B as the dashboard. decay: 0.8 is the alternative form (80 % of the remaining distance kept every frame at 30 fps).
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards.bento`, `fx/Cards.Bento`
- **Timing:** 44 f on E.snapOut (42-60 f); delays 0-18 f.
- **Use when:** A panel becomes a dashboard, a list becomes a grid, an overview opens.
- **Avoid when:** The tiles carry long text that would be cut by the moving boxes mid-read.

### Calm hold marked only by small label pops

`dv-quiet-hold-label-pops` · pacing and structure · accent · energy calm · any

A grid holds almost still for several seconds and the only events are three small labels popping next to tiles about a second apart: rest that still has a pulse.

- **Build:** living hold + Words pop for labels. Anatomy: Camera creep only (0.98-1.0); label pops 1 s apart. Sound: A bubble pop and a click on the pops; a low hit.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** 344 f hold; pops 50-70 f apart.
- **Use when:** After a busy run; to let a layout be read.
- **Avoid when:** Holds longer than about 6 s.

### Card or model turns 180 deg with the edge-on frame on the beat

`dv-object-flip-turn` · depth and 3d · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

A card rotates about its axis in perspective (long ease-in, quicker ease-out) and goes edge-on exactly on the downbeat, swapping its face there; a 3D model inside a card turns from front to side to back.

- **Build:** Build: <Flip3D at={flipAt(beat, {})} x y w h front back> (fx/Flip): a 180 deg turn on E.whipBuild (65 f, peak speed near 58 %) whose edge-on frame lands on the beat and swaps the faces there (declared a morph seam). Anatomy: Peak 8.4 deg/f at 58 %; face swap on the edge-on frame. Sound: The edge-on frame on the downbeat (-37 ms).
- **Primitive:** `fx/Flip.Flip3D`
- **Timing:** 65 f; model turn 28 f.
- **Use when:** Revealing the other side; turning a product.
- **Avoid when:** Flips with readable text on both sides at once.

### Device hinges open and its world pops around it

`dv-device-hinge-open` · depth and 3d · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

A thin slab hinges open into a laptop (screen growing 44 -> 466 px with a slight yaw), then an envelope rises from behind the screen and a notification dot and a chat pill pop around it.

- **Build:** Build: <Flip3D kind="hinge" at x y w h front> (fx/Flip): the screen turns -90 -> 0 deg about its bottom edge on E.snapOut (22 f); the satellites pop with Cards or MicroUI after it. Anatomy: Hinge rotateX quad-out; satellites pop 6, 4, 6 f in sequence. Sound: A bubble pop on the envelope. Materials: The dark screen picks up a soft diagonal reflection (white at about 45 % with a cool tint, band at about 60 deg) that grows and slides across as the device yaws toward the camera, strongest mid-turn, fading as the camera pushes in.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Flip.Flip3D`
- **Materials:** The dark screen picks up a soft diagonal reflection (white at about 45 % with a cool tint, band at about 60 deg) that grows and slides across as the device yaws toward the camera, strongest mid-turn, fading as the camera pushes in.
- **Timing:** Hinge 22 f; satellites 10-15 f each.
- **Use when:** Introducing a device or an app in context.
- **Avoid when:** Too many satellites.

### Exploded view: panels push out, spin, collapse

`dv-exploded-view` · depth and 3d · signature · energy medium · launch, sting

A face panel lifts off a 3D object and floats, the inner panels push outward into an exploded cube inside a larger box, the camera spins slowly in isometric, then everything collapses back.

- **Build:** Recipe: CSS 3D faces (preserve-3d) offset along normals by one progress value; spin as the container's rotateY. Anatomy: Panels offset along their normals; isometric camera spin on a sine-out; collapse on an ease-in. Sound: None needed.
- **Timing:** Explode 78 f, spin 98 f, collapse 35 f.
- **Use when:** Explaining an architecture, layers or what is inside.
- **Avoid when:** Flat 2D products.
